{{Other uses|RMS (disambiguation){{!}}RMS}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''signal magnitude area''' (abbreviated '''SMA''' or '''sma''') is a [[statistics|statistical]] measure of the [[magnitude (mathematics)|magnitude]] of a varying quantity.

==Definition==
The SMA value of a set of values (or a [[continuous-time]] [[waveform]]) is the [[Normalization (statistics)|normalized]] [[integral]] of the original values.
<ref>{{cite web|title=Matlab compute Normalized Signal Magnitude area|url=https://stackoverflow.com/questions/19702753/matlab-compute-normalized-signal-magnitude-area}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=2008 30th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society|arxiv=1107.4417|year=2008|last1=Chung|first1=W. Y.|last2=Purwar|first2=A.|last3=Sharma|first3=A.|chapter=Frequency domain approach for activity classification using accelerometer |pages=1120–3|doi=10.1109/IEMBS.2008.4649357 |pmid=19162860 |isbn=978-1-4244-1814-5 }}</ref>

In the case of a set of ''n'' values <math>\{x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n\}</math> matching a time length ''T'', the SMA

:<math>
x_\text{sma} = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i
</math>

In the continuous domain, we have for example, with a 3-axis signal with an offset correction ''a'' for each axis, the following equation:<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.rehab.research.va.gov/jour/2013/509/jrrd-2012-12-0233.html|title = Classifying prosthetic use via accelerometry in persons with transtibial amputations|date = 2013|accessdate = 2014-10-14|website = [[Journal of Rehabilitation Research & Development]]|publisher = U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs|last = |first = |last2 = |first2 = }}</ref>

:<math>
f_\text{sma}= {1 \over T} \int_0^T |x(t)-a_x|+|y(t)-a_y|+|z(t)-a_z| \, dt
</math>
